title: Capreomycin (historical injectable)
dek: A cyclic peptide, not an aminoglycoside, that still wrecks hearing and kidneys. tlyA loss is the signature. Retired from preferred DR-TB; old XDR papers used it as the second injectable tick.
story: Capreomycin is a tuberactinomycin (with viomycin) injected in the MDR era when kanamycin failed or as the “second injectable” that minted old XDR. It is not an aminoglycoside chemically, but the toxicity rhyme is the same: irreversible hearing loss, renal injury, electrolyte wasting.

tlyA encodes a 2'-O-methyltransferase for rRNA; loss-of-function confers CAP (and viomycin) resistance. rrs 1401 also raises CAP MIC. eis promoter-up does not equal CAP-R. Do not auto-translate “injectable R” from a KM eis allele onto CAP.

WHO preferred regimens do not start with CAP. If a salvage committee reaches for it, they have already lost BDQ/LZD/FQ options and should say that out loud, with audiometry scheduled before the first dose.
deepTitle: Why the chemistry still confuses pipelines
deep: Some software buckets KM/AMK/CAP as one “injectable” bit. Unbucket them.
Viomycin is not stocked; tlyA still appears in catalogues.
CAP does not treat NTM the way AMK sometimes does. Different object.
Pregnancy: injectables stay off for fetal ototoxicity.

visual.caption: CAP is tlyA + some rrs, not eis. Old XDR used CAP/KM as the injectable tick; 2021 XDR does not.
